title: Arranger influences and Mary Lou Williams
summary: No single arranger influenced her; she learned from Al Wilson and Paul Barnes and respected Mary Lou Williams.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When you started writing for big bands at a very early age, was there any particular arranger that you were aware of or any particular band whose arrangements appealed to you that made you want to write?

Well, I can't really say so. I think I liked the idea of writing and had a good sense of harmony and a good sense of doing this type of thing, and being around people that were doing it. These guys were writing all the time, particularly this Al Wilson, and as I mentioned, Paul Barnes. These guys were always writing and it just sort of struck me that this is something that I would enjoy doing, see. And as I say, Mary Lou Williams was of course writing at the same time, but I can't say that -- I really can't say that I was really influenced by her. However, I certainly have great respect and admiration for her, because she was one of the first women, I
think, to really make a name for herself as an arranger.
